A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CPPO. All 16 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support matching content across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CPPO-versus-GRPO accuracy and training-time measurements, pruning and component ablations, training curves and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds three-run summaries, other RL algorithm comparisons, and evaluations with larger and different model backbones.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 3 add DAPO+CPPO and DrGRPO+CPPO training variants, extending the pruning approach to other policy optimizers. The original CPPO objective, absolute-advantage selection, reward functions and allocation strategy remain. Appendix B principally clarifies implementation rather than establishing a changed original algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on GSM8K and MATH and evaluate on their test subsets plus AMC2023 and AIME2024. The added experiments vary models, frameworks and optimizers within this retained mathematical task coverage.

E2.justification: v1's principal comparison is against GRPO. v2 adds evaluated DAPO and DrGRPO comparisons, including their CPPO combinations, in Table 3, and REINFORCE++ and PPO without KL divergence in Table 11. This substantially broadens the competing optimization methods considered.

E3.justification: v2 adds experiments on verl, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on MATH, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on GSM8K, and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on GSM8K. Table 11 also introduces a PPO comparison using group size 1 versus 16 for the other algorithms. These expand experimental configurations substantially; the existing decoding rules, metrics and principal hyperparameters remain.

E4.justification: The completion-count study, matched-question-batch comparison, pruning-metric ablation and component ablation retain their evidence. The reward curves and case studies are moved into Appendices H–J, with the same examples and findings. The added model and optimizer benchmark scores do not introduce a distinct diagnostic or stress test.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 newly specify three independent training runs and report means and standard deviations for GSM8K/MATH accuracy, training time and CPPO speedup. v1 provides point estimates without run-count or uncertainty reporting. This materially strengthens statistical reporting, although the OOD columns and added comparison tables remain point estimates; v1's actual run count is unspecified.

E6.justification: Main-table point estimates are replaced by three-run summaries: for example, GSM8K CPPO accuracy at 87.5% pruning changes from 80.41% to 80.01±0.38%, and speedup at 93.75% changes from 8.32 to 7.98±0.23. Tables 3 and 8–11 add substantial results, including DAPO+CPPO retaining 78.01% accuracy with 1.78× speedup. These additions use distinct configurations and do not establish gains over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The explanation following Eq. (7) corrects the positive-advantage clipping condition from probability ratio < 1+epsilon to > 1+epsilon. This repairs a mathematical condition; the objectives, gradient derivation and reward definitions otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise headline speedups from 8.32×/3.51× to 7.98×/3.48× for GSM8K/MATH. The conclusion adds qualifications about a suitable pruning rate and sometimes preserving or improving accuracy. The central contributions remain completion pruning and dynamic allocation.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly explains that CPPO does not accelerate completion generation, limiting speedup when generation dominates, and identifies inference acceleration as complementary. It updates the model-scale limitation and future priorities. Appendix E also explains the smaller GSM8K accuracy improvement for the 7B model through its higher initial accuracy and limited remaining headroom.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds pseudocode specifying pruning-dependent batch and step counts and explains that implementation allocates questions before pruning to exploit parallel generation and prefix sharing. v2 also documents use of verl. These clarify reproducibility, while the principal hyperparameters, reward specifications, prompt templates and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for DAPO, DrGRPO, REINFORCE++, HybridFlow/verl, speculative sampling and EAGLE. These support targeted positioning of CPPO as compatible with other optimizers and complementary to inference acceleration. The existing related-work narrative is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendix organization are substantially reworked: stability discussion, case studies and completion examples move from the main text into Appendices H–J; algorithm documentation receives Appendix B; and references move before the appendices. Experimental subsections are reorganized and limitations rewritten, although much introductory and methodological prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds five experimental tables and an algorithm display, reformats Tables 1–2 for uncertainty reporting, and relocates several existing displays. v1's two-panel reward Figure 4 becomes enlarged separate Figures 5–6 in the appendix, while its completion examples and case tables are redistributed. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves variability in its central speed–accuracy comparisons unreported and evaluates a narrow optimizer/model selection. v2's three-run summaries in Tables 1–2 and broader comparisons in Tables 3 and 8–11 substantially improve the evidence for reliability and applicability. Appendix B clarifies implementation, and Section 5 identifies the generation-time bottleneck. Uncertainty reporting remains incomplete for supplementary comparisons, but the revision materially strengthens empirical support and qualification of the claims.
